subject: Direct Vector borrowed-call forwarding and repeated loop borrows
claim: The candidate emitter preserves original Vector slot identity at direct borrowed calls. The 3,851-byte regression module is deterministic and identical on Windows and Debian, verifies completely, and returns 42. It covers parameter forwarding, exclusive-to-immutable forwarding, duplicate immutable arguments, nested and named argument evaluation, and 128 loop borrows. Eleven bytecode mutations reject at verifier and runner boundaries; eleven invalid sources reject before publication. Existing owned-call and scope-release fixtures remain valid, with each module 14 bytes smaller. Nine owned Option/Result scenarios, eight copied-payload mutations, and two invalid-budget sources also pass per host.

Existing candidate WVB 1.40 parameter-length reads and WVB 1.26 borrowed-call semantics are unchanged. No bytecode version, verifier rule, or runtime contract was relaxed.
Linux packages reuse Windows-generated WVB/native images. This is paired-host execution, not independent Linux compiler reconstruction or full cross-host Qualification.

No installed identity, bootstrap promotion, native minor-40 lowering, browser, OS, or release artifact is claimed. The full automatic plan (10 native owners, 3,450 expected seconds and 13,800 maximum seconds) was not run; existing explicit focused selectors were chosen for causal coverage and to avoid redundant cold construction.

Initial full current-compiler construction reached its 60-minute cap and did not pass. Completed products and authenticated caches were retained. Explicit focused construction/packaging and final checks then ran within a second approved 45-minute batch; no full compiler-cache publication is claimed.

An initial changed-emitter source build rejected duplicate local names; these were corrected before the recorded passing construction. The new projected-payload negative test initially rejected a missing and then misordered dependency; its corrected final case reaches Unsupported_operation before publication.

An initial task-local Linux packaging helper appended extra service fragments to two image-cache directories. Its postcheck failed; only the new sidecars were moved aside, original checkpoint hashes were revalidated, and resulting packages matched the prior recorded identities. Subsequent packages used private image copies and passed postchecks.

Per-function planning uses existing bounds of 4,096 operations, 4,096 temporaries and 64 slots, with at most 66,304 logical retained table bytes. Immutable updates copy bounded buffers. No whole-workflow peak memory measurement or timing improvement claim is made; emitted regression modules remain below 8,192 bytes.

Pure runtime-only Foundation borrow cases were not repeated because the runtime products are byte-identical to the earlier paired-host record. Their evidence is reused only for those unchanged inputs, not as verification of the new compiler.
AI review found and helped close the projected-payload provenance boundary and golden-identity updates. No human inspection, external audit, or independent reproduction is claimed.

The plan checker initially rejected the additional compiler call site introduced by the legacy regressions. Its exact inventory expectation was updated from 88 to the measured 89; the final plan check passed.
